title: Explore SAI-93 as a single crystal and biomass hauler
context: The owner proposed replacing Yushi with a flying SAI-93 that collects both resources. This is an exploration request; the shipping resource system remains unchanged.
outcome: A shared flying hauler is viable, but a direct substitution with current SAI-93 tuning is not equivalent. In the existing rover transport FSM, a 6000 kg pile on a straight 350 m one-way route banks in 48.1 s with Yushi (one trip), 340.0 s with current SAI-93 (ten trips), or 43.0 s with SAI-93 flight speed and Yushi capacity/loading rates (one trip). A prototype should first preserve hauling throughput, then evaluate the loss of ground-route escort and disabled-rover rescue, shared dispatch priority, separate cargo accounting and depot delivery. No vehicle replacement or economy tuning was applied.
alternatives: Retain the current split: Yushi for biomass, SAI-93 for crystals.
Prototype one aircraft with separate mineral and biomass job queues and explicit cargo type, using comparable biomass hauling throughput.
A direct replacement with the current 600 kg SAI hold would reduce income substantially.
evidence: src/content/rover.js: capacity 6000 kg, harvest 400 kg/s, unload 1000 kg/s, speed 26 m/s.
src/content/minerals.js: capacity 600 kg, harvest 75 kg/s, unload 150 kg/s, speed 32 m/s.

Measured using src/domain/rover-run.js createRoverRun/dispatch/stepRover at dt .05 with one 6000 kg pile, straight 350 m legs, unlimited depot storage and no threat. The matched variant changes only capacity, harvestRate and unloadRate to Yushi values.
This simplified comparison excludes terrain detours, takeoff/landing, enemy pressure, flare expiry and seepage; it is a transport comparison, not a campaign balance result.
